KeyChord Reference

Press chord keys together, then release them to type a syllable or word.

Open Practice to try chords with hints. The keyboard overlay in Settings keeps the mapping visible while you type in other apps.

Getting started

  1. Open Practice to type locally with hints. No permissions are needed. To type in other apps, choose Enable Typing in Other Apps in the menu and allow Accessibility access.
  2. Tap the right ⌥ Option key to turn chord typing on. The menu bar shows English next to the keyboard icon. Tap it again to type normally.
  3. Press all the keys of a chord, then let go. You don't need to press them at exactly the same moment: a chord is everything you press before all keys are up. KeyChord adds the space before each word.
the=ETth+Be

Keyboard shortcuts with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ always work as usual, and chord typing pauses by itself in password fields.

The keyboard

Every key has a meaning, shown in large type below; the letter printed on the key is in the corner. A syllable is its start, its vowel and its end, pressed together:

  • the left hand plays the consonants at the start,
  • the thumbs play the vowel on the bottom row,
  • the right hand plays the consonants at the end.

Small type at the bottom of a key says what it does when pressed alone, when that is something else: O alone adds the ending “ed”, for example. The pictures show the MacBook Pro's US keyboard; with another layout, use the key in the same place.

Syllables

Use the word's spelling: combine its start letters, vowel and end letters in one chord. Leave out the parts a word doesn't have. Release every key before starting the next chord.

sat=Ss+Ca+Jt
stop=TSst+Vo+Pp

Capitals and punctuation

  • After . ? and ! the next word gets a capital by itself.

  • '. is a full stop without the capital after it, for “Mr. and Mrs.”
  • With Caps Lock on, everything you chord comes out in capitals.

Punctuation attaches to the word before it, and opening brackets and quotes to the word after. The opening double-quote chord also closes an open quote, without adding a space before it:

A long word takes a chord for each part. KeyChord puts a space before every chord, so press the space bar (Space) together with each chord after the first: that chord joins onto the word instead. Whichever thumb isn't on a vowel presses it.

A few chords can't take the space bar, because they already use six keys or the keyboard would drop that combination. Hold ⇧ Shift instead for those; Practice says when.

Letters and numbers

Any word can be spelled letter by letter: ' plus the key printed with the letter. Add ; for a capital. Letters join together without spaces.

Fixing mistakes

\ undoes the last chord, and you can press it again to go further back. ⌫ Delete works as usual.

Typing without chords

Tap the right ⌥ Option key, type as usual, and tap it again to go back to chords. The space bar (Space) pressed alone types a space in both. Practice says when a piece of text has no chord.

Practice

Choose Words, Lessons, or Voice Practice from the Practice submenu in the menu bar. Open Practice resumes your last activity. Lessons teach the English and C++ course and keep your saved progress. Words offers short word sessions or a timer. Toggle chord hints with ⇧⌘H to practice from memory. Right Option switches between chords and ordinary typing.

Voice reads a word, waits for your typed chord answer, gives spoken feedback, and moves on after a correct answer. Use ⇧⌘R to hear it again and ⇧⌘H to hear the chord keys. No microphone is needed.

Custom chords

Open Custom Chords to give a word, phrase, or symbol your own key combination. Record keys or choose Find unused chord, enter the text, and choose a language. The before-and-after preview shows each affected combination and language, including its original meaning. Try chord tests the unsaved draft locally; press it twice to check spacing, or choose English or C++ when using both.

Save chord or Replace chord applies your changes. Turn off Enabled when saved and save to restore the original mapping while keeping your customization. Remove also restores the original mapping. The library labels chords On, Off, or Needs repair; select a chord to see why it needs attention.

Choose Words & phrases for normal word spacing and capitalization, or No added spaces for text that attaches on both sides without extra spaces. Caps Lock still applies. Built-in actions and Space keep their existing jobs.

When a chord doesn't work

Some keyboards cannot detect certain keys held together. Practice suggests alternatives for combinations that the available keyboard model predicts will fail. Custom Chords checks these combinations before saving. Other keyboards may behave differently; if a chord doesn't register, try fewer keys or choose a different combination.
